headline: NovaMind v3 Goes Live — Neural-Mesh Promises Total Sensory Integration
body:
NovaMind launched its third-generation Brain-Computer Interface platform at a packed consumer event in The Circuit's Apex Pavilion on Tuesday, unveiling the v3 Neural-Mesh system to an audience that included corponation executives, licensed medical providers, and approximately 8,000 registered consumers who had camped outside since Sunday. The Neural-Mesh abandons the traditional hub-and-spoke node architecture of previous NovaMind systems in favor of a distributed filament web that spreads across 34 cortical zones, enabling simultaneous sensory overlay, memory indexing, and real-time translation in 214 languages. NovaMind's partnership with Axiom — which provides the secure data infrastructure underlying v3's cloud functions — was prominently featured throughout the presentation.

Early adopters describe the upgrade experience as disorienting but transformative. 'It took about 48 hours before my brain stopped fighting it,' said Meridian Circuit District resident Nkechi Albrecht-Sato, one of the 500 Beta participants. 'After that, it was like someone turned the resolution of reality up.' The v3 platform's signature feature — called Presence — allows users to project a haptic-interactive avatar into any shared neural space, effectively enabling full-body digital embodiment without leaving a physical location. Corporate clients have already pre-purchased 1.2 million enterprise licenses.

Not everyone in the auditorium was celebrating. A small protest outside the Apex Pavilion, organized by the Wishing Well movement, drew roughly 200 demonstrators who held signs reading 'Your Mind Is Not a Product' and 'Unplug Before You Can't.' Wishing Well speaker Ezra Fontaine-Ibo told gathered press that NovaMind v3 represents 'the final frontier of corporate colonization — the interior of the human self.' The Federal Remnant's Office of Neural Regulation approved v3 for commercial sale on a 4-1 board vote, with the dissenting member citing unresolved questions about the Axiom data-sharing clause embedded in the user agreement.
aftermath: Within 90 days of launch, a class-action lawsuit alleged that Axiom was harvesting and selling v3 users' subvocalized private thoughts captured incidentally by the Neural-Mesh's language processing layer.
runner_relevance: The v3 launch created immediate demand for runners on both sides of a corporate information war. Competing corponations — particularly Sterling-Nakamura and Tessera — contracted data-retrieval specialists to pull NovaMind's proprietary Neural-Mesh schematics before Axiom could lock them behind patent walls. The Axiom data-harvesting controversy spawned a cottage industry of counter-surveillance runners hired by high-value clients — executives, politicians, Iron Lotus leadership — to physically escort NovaMind technicians during installation and audit the hardware for unauthorized capture nodes. The Wishing Well, flush with donations after the lawsuit broke, began hiring courier runners to distribute analog 'mesh-block' devices through The Shelf.
